newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says U.S. blocks contract to supply pesticide.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says U.S. blocks contract to supply pesticide.

text.p: The United States has blocked a contract to supply Iraq with anti-mosquito pesticide under its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations, Iraq's Health Minister Umeed Madahat Mubarak said on Tuesday.

"The United States envoy at the United Nations sanctions committee (on Iraq) has put on hold a contract to supply the health ministry with pesticide to combat mosquitoes to prevent the spread of malaria," Mubarak said in a statement carried by the Iraqi News Agency.
He said Iraq wanted to use the pesticide contracted with a British firm in three Iraqi provinces, Daiyla, Nineveh and Ta'meem. He did not say whether malaria was spreading in these areas.

Under the deal, which went into effect in December, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food and medicine for its population, hit by U.N. sanctions imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait. The deal is due for review in June.

Iraq has complained frequently that Washington has prevented the supplies from reaching the country within a reasonable period of time while oil sales moved quickly. The U.S. envoy to the United Nations, Bill Richardson, has voiced misgivings about the deal.
"Blocking the contract by the American representative would threaten public health as malaria has spread in northern Iraq, Iran and southern Turkey," Mubarak added.
